MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: GENERAL REQUIREMENTS: You MUST have successfully completed a full course of study in a school of law accredited by the American Bar Association (ABA) and have the first professional law degree (LLB or JD). In addition, at the time of application, you must provide proof, dated within four months of application, of "active" status with a bar of the highest court of a State, U.S. commonwealth, U.S. territory, or the District of Columbia. On-line information is allowed as long as it shows that you are in "active" status. Specialized Experience: In addition to the basic requirement, you must have professional legal experience in excess of three (3) years that commensurate with the position's duties and responsibilities. KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES (KSAs): Your qualifications will be evaluated on the basis of your level of knowledge, skills, abilities and/or competencies in the following areas: Knowledge of national and international laws, regulations, policies, and ethics related to cybersecurity to provide legal analysis and decisions to oversight and compliance personnel. Knowledge of a wide range of legal concepts, principles, practices, statutory and case law, and regulatory and administrative decisions in highly specialized and complex legal fields. Knowledge of ethics laws and regulations (including OGE, DoW, and Air Force) and the ability to apply them to complex, novel, and time sensitive law enforcement and counterintelligence situations. Knowledge of federal criminal law, the Uniform Code of Military Justice (UCMJ), information technology law, and administrative law, including DoW, Air Force, and DC3 operating procedures. Skill in conducting legal research and the ability to write clear, concise, and comprehensive legal briefs, memoranda, and instructional materials from a variety of sources. Ability to instruct, educate, and present briefings, lectures, and legal arguments to top-level audiences in administrative, judicial, and quasi-judicial proceedings. Ability to supervise, mentor, and guide others toward goal accomplishment while collaborating with internal and external attorneys on complex legal issues. At the time of application, you must provide proof, dated within four months of application, of "active" status and in good standing with a bar of the highest court of a State, US commonwealth, US territory, or the District of Columbia. On-line information is allowed as long as it shows that you are in "active" status and dated within four months of application. PART-TIME OR UNPAID EXPERIENCE: Credit will be given for appropriate unpaid and or part-time work. You must clearly identify the duties and responsibilities in each position held and the total number of hours per week. VOLUNTEER WORK EXPERIENCE: Refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service Programs (i.e., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student and social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge and skills that can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience. Conditions of Employment Continued: The attorney must be a graduate if an accredited law school and be admitted to the practice of law before the highest court of a state, territory, possession, or commonwealth of the United States and must maintain an active law license in at least one of the identified jurisdictions. This position has been designated by the Air Force as a Testing Designated Position (TDP) under the Air Force Civilian Drug Demand Reduction Program. Employee must pass initial and periodic short notice drug testing. Illegal drug use by employees in sensitive positions presents a clear threat to the mission of the Air Force, national security, and public safety.

Details.JobSummary: The primary purpose of this position is to serve as the Department of Defense Cyber Crime Center (DC3), Senior Judge Advocate (JA) providing expert legal guidance, direction, primary authority, and experiencedsupervision of personnel to support DC3 operations. Provides attorney-advisory guidance to the DC3 Executive Director and DC3 workforce composed of government military, civilian, and contractors across a widerange of disciplines.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The mission of the United States Air Force is: To fly, fight, and win ... Airpower anytime, anywhere. To achieve that mission, the Air Force has a vision of Global Vigilance, Global Reach and Global Power. That vision orbits around three core competencies: Developing Airmen, Technology-to-Warfighting and Integrating Operations. Core competencies and distinctive capabilities are based on a shared commitment to three core values -- integrity first, service before self, and excellence in all we do.
MajorDuties: Senior Cyber Legal Advisor providing advice, counsel and advocacy in support of the DC3 mission regarding cyber law. Operates independently, with a wide degree of latitude for the exercise of professional judgment and initiative advising on relevant cyber law areas to include the following: Use of cyber forensics and forensics-enabled analytics to enhance DC3 support of customer missions in the areas of military operations, law enforcement, intelligence and cybersecurity; Defense Industrial Base cybersecurity activities; DoW cyber vulnerability management; and, establishment and sustainment of authoritative data repositories for cyber information sharing among supported DoW and federal agencies. Senior Criminal Litigation Support Attorney reviewing requests and supporting legal bases for forensic digital evidence analysis by DC3 Cyber Forensics Laboratory. Prepares detailed responses to complex pretrial discovery requests utilizing law and procedures for both military and civilian criminal court proceedings; prepares expert witnesses for testimony in adversarial judicial proceedings; and advises prosecutors and investigators with regard to digital evidence issues during investigations, undercover operations, at trial and in appellate proceedings. Senior Judge Advocate providing advisement of policies and practices, and legal reviews on Ethics, Intelligence Oversight and Acquisition, Intellectual Property and Federal Appropriations. Serves as the Ethics Attorney for DC3 on behalf of the Designated Agency Ethics Official (DAEO); provides ethics advisory opinions on entire range of ethics-related matters; conducts and monitors the accuracy and quality of training provided to the agency; ensures compliance with financial disclosure and training requirements for entire agency; and ensures agency compliance with any ethics program reporting requirements. Exercises supervisory personnel management responsibilities. Advises and provides counsel to employees regarding policies, procedures, and directives of management. Selects or recommends selection of candidates for vacancies, promotions, details, and reassignments in consideration of skills and qualifications, mission requirements, and EEO and diversity objectives.
Details.Education: Must be a graduate of a law school accredited by the American Bar Association, and be currently licensed as an attorney, in active (or equivalent) status and in good standing, with the bar of a U.S. state, territory, or commonwealth. The attorney must maintain such bar membership in at least one jurisdiction during the entire course of employment with the Air Force.

serves as a current operations expert providing continuous analysis, evaluation, oversight, situational awareness, and mission status reporting for Offensive and Defensive Cyberspace and Information operations.

Serves as the focal point for receiving taskings, requirements, and Request for Information (RFI) from higher headquarters.

Army CES positions apply Veteran's Preference to preference eligible candidates, as defined by Section 2108 of Title 5 U.S.C., in accordance with the procedures provided in DoD Instruction 1400.25, Volume 3005, "CES Employment and Placement". Specialized experience would be demonstrated by 1) Coordinating the integration of Operation Information Environment (OIE) capabilities into active and future joint military operations; 2) Assisting in conducting OIE planning during time-sensitive events; 3) Implementing the oversight of daily operational workflows to ensure activities comply with established technical, policy, and legal constraints. A graduate of the Joint Information Planners Course Phase 2 (or equivalent) and of a joint or service accredited Military Deception/Defense Deception Activity course is preferred; ideal candidates will be graduates of the Psychological Operations Qualification Course (POQC) or equivalent. This position is in the Supervision/Management Work Category at the Senior Work Level within the CES Occupational Structure.

Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Civilian employees serve a vital role in supporting the Army mission. They provide the skills that are not readily available in the military, but crucial to support military operations. The Army integrates the talents and skills of its military and civilian members to form a Total Army. Looking to make a difference? Join our team! Army Materiel Command (AMC) is the Army's primary logistics and sustainment command, responsible for managing the global supply chain and ensuring installation and materiel readiness across the Total Force. AMC is one of the Army's largest commands with nearly 165,000 military, Army Civilian and contractor employees, impacting all 50 states and more than 150 countries. Since 1962, AMC has played a significant role in supplying our forces during wars, conflicts and contingencies, and providing humanitarian aid and disaster relief. From managing the Army's global supply chain to providing quality of life programs for Soldiers and families; from providing financial management and contracting capabilities to leading the way in data analytics, AMC's missions are wide ranging and critical. AMC's workforce is at the core of the command's support to the Warfighter. If you are ready to take your career to the next level and be part of a culture that puts people first, we have an extensive array of career paths available. Join today and be the power behind ensuring the best equipped and sustained fighting force in the world.
MajorDuties: Assess the effectiveness of existing cybersecurity controls to recommend improvements
Review cyber directives and policies to ensure compliance with established cybersecurity standards.
Conduct crisis action planning for cyberspace operations to render appropriate effects across the surface transportation enterprise.
Develop operational procedures regarding cyber effects to ensure alignment with DoD, USTRANSCOM, and/or Army policies.
Utilize advanced systems research and planning methods to guide long-range cybersecurity initiatives.
Integrate information management technologies to optimize the development and management of cyber defense systems.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: DKI APCSS seeks qualified candidates at the Associate Professor or Professor level specializing in China Military Strategy and Future Warfare to join the Department of Strategic Deterrence. The successful candidate will educate civilian and military security practitioners on China's military strategy, People's Liberation Army (PLA) modernization, and the changing character of warfare and deterrence in the Indo-Pacific. The position focuses on how PLA strategy, force development, operational concepts, joint campaigning, and emerging technologies affect deterrence, crisis management, escalation, defense planning, and regional security. The position requires particular depth of understanding of the PLA as a military institution and fighting force, while situating Chinese military developments within the broader political, strategic, and technological context of the Indo-Pacific. The successful candidate will help practitioners assess how evolving PLA capabilities and concepts shape the challenges of deterring aggression, managing crises, controlling escalation, and preparing for future warfare. Candidates are not expected to enter the position with expertise across every element of this portfolio. DKI APCSS seeks individuals with demonstrated expertise in relevant areas and the intellectual ability and professional commitment to develop broader expertise in Chinese military affairs, strategic deterrence, crisis management, and future warfare. Faculty members at DKI APCSS are expected to be more than subject-matter experts. They serve as educators, facilitators, curriculum designers, action officers, researchers, mentors, and institutional leaders. Faculty plan and execute executive education courses, workshops, strategic dialogues, and regional engagements; develop and facilitate curriculum; conduct policy-relevant research; and build relationships with security professionals throughout the Indo-Pacific. Essential Criteria An advanced degree in international relations, security studies, political science, strategic studies, military studies, China studies, Asian studies, public policy, or a related discipline. A doctorate or other terminal degree is preferred. Demonstrated substantive knowledge, research, or professional experience related to Chinese military affairs, PLA modernization, Chinese military strategy, strategic deterrence, crisis management, future warfare, or a closely related field. Demonstrated ability to conduct rigorous research, analyze contemporary security issues, and produce scholarly or policy-relevant work. Demonstrated ability to teach, facilitate, and mentor adult learners from diverse professional, national, and cultural backgrounds. Ability to communicate complex military, strategic, political, and technological issues clearly to practitioner audiences. Strong organizational skills and demonstrated ability to plan, coordinate, and execute complex projects or programs. Ability to work effectively as a collegial, collaborative, and team-oriented faculty member. Ability to use contemporary technologies and digital tools in research, teaching, collaboration, and program execution. Demonstrated commitment to the DKI APCSS mission and to advancing security cooperation and understanding throughout the Indo-Pacific. Desired Criteria Demonstrated expertise, research, or professional experience in one or more of the following areas: People's Liberation Army strategy, doctrine, and modernization Chinese military strategy and operational concepts PLA joint campaigning and joint operations Chinese force development and defense modernization Deterrence and strategic stability Crisis management and escalation Military innovation and adaptation Future warfare Artificial intelligence, autonomous systems, and human-machine integration Space and cyber operations Advanced weapons and emerging military technologies Multi-domain operations Taiwan Strait and First Island Chain security dynamics Chinese military activities and security relationships throughout the Indo-Pacific Additional desired experience includes: Ability to conduct research using Chinese-language primary or secondary sources. Chinese-language proficiency appropriate to the candidate's research or professional specialization. Research, professional, military, government, or field experience involving China or Indo-Pacific defense and security affairs. Experience working with or studying defense ministries, military organizations, combatant commands, intelligence organizations, policy institutions, universities, or allied and partner governments. Experience in teaching, facilitation, executive education, strategic engagement, policy dialogue, exercises, or multinational workshops Experience building professional networks and fostering collaboration among individuals from diverse national, institutional, and professional backgrounds. Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., professional, philanthropic, religious, spiritual, community, student, social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment.

Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The Daniel K. Inouye Asia-Pacific Center for Security Studies (DKI APCSS) is a U.S. Department of War institution dedicated to advancing security throughout the Indo-Pacific through executive education, strategic dialogue, research, and regional collaboration. Located in Honolulu, Hawaii, the Center educates, connects, and empowers civilian and military security professionals to address complex regional and transnational security challenges. Through executive courses, workshops, strategic dialogues, policy engagements, and scholarly activities, DKI APCSS develops enduring professional networks, strengthens institutional capacity, and advances a free, open, secure, and prosperous Indo-Pacific.
MajorDuties: You will design, develop, and teach executive education addressing Chinese military strategy, PLA modernization, deterrence and crisis management, joint campaigning, military innovation, and the changing character of warfare.

You will analyze PLA strategy, doctrine, force development, operational concepts, capabilities, and modernization and their implications for deterrence, crisis stability, escalation, and Indo-Pacific security.

You will examine how emerging technologies—including artificial intelligence, autonomous systems, advanced weapons, space, cyber, and other capabilities—may affect Chinese military operations, deterrence, escalation, and future warfare.

You will develop educational programs and activities that help practitioners analyze evolving PLA capabilities, assess implications for deterrence and crisis management, and examine alternative approaches to consequential security challenges.
You will lead and support Center activities, including executive education courses, workshops, policy dialogues, senior-leader engagements, strategic visits, and international partnerships.
You will serve as an action officer responsible for planning and executing courses, workshops, strategic dialogues, and regional engagements from concept development through execution and assessment.
You will develop curriculum, instructional materials, case studies, simulations, and experiential-learning activities appropriate to diverse civilian and military audiences.
You will teach and facilitate seminars and collaborative learning among security practitioners from throughout the Indo-Pacific.
You will conduct research and publish scholarly and policy-relevant work on Chinese military affairs, strategic deterrence, military modernization, crisis management, escalation, and future warfare.
You will engage regional defense and security practitioners, academic institutions, and partner organizations to deepen understanding of Chinese military developments and their regional implications.
You will develop and maintain substantive expertise necessary to support executive education, regional engagement, academic partnerships, public outreach, and strategic initiatives.

You will collaborate across departments and disciplines to integrate China and PLA expertise into College programming, addressing alliances and partnerships, regional security architecture, resilience, security cooperation, and other challenges.
You will mentor Fellows and contribute to their professional and intellectual development.
You will contribute to the effective administration and institutional development of the College.
You will maintain productive, professional, respectful, and collegial relationships with leadership, faculty, staff, Fellows, and regional partners.

Additional information about transcripts is in this document. Specialized experience is progressively responsible intelligence-related security work directly related to the position being filled. Creditable experience may include previous military experience, experience gained in the private sector or in another government agency as long as it was at a level at least equivalent to the next lower band in the series. To qualify based on your experience, your resume must describe at least one (1) year of experience equivalent to at least the GG-13 grade level in the Federal service which prepared you to do the work in this job. Specialized experience is defined as: 1. Experience with Intelligence Production Management and setting long range estimate development and projections; 2. Intelligence Requirements Management;AND 3.Experience with the all-source intelligence process and procedures applicable to Intelligence Preparation of the Battlefield analysis. Progressively responsible experience is that which has included intelligence-related research, analysis, collections and /or operations. This experience should have included intelligence analysis and/or production, intelligence collection and/or operations, counterintelligence, or threat support directly related to the position to be filled. This experience should demonstrate: Knowledge of intelligence processes, cycle and organizations; Knowledge of and/or ability to use research tools such as library holdings, photographs, statistics, graphics and maps; Knowledge of the systems, procedures and methods of analyzing, compiling, reporting and disseminating intelligence data; and/or Knowledge of organization(s) for and methods of collecting and analyzing intelligence data.

Details.JobSummary: About the Position: This position is in the Defense Civilian Intelligence Personnel System (DCIPS). Employees occupying DCIPS positions are in the Excepted Service and must adhere to U.S. Code, Title 10, as well as Department of Defense Instruction 1400.25. This position is located at the Joint Force Headquarters - Cyber at Fort Gordon, GA.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Civilian employees serve a vital role in supporting the Army mission. They provide the skills that are not readily available in the military, but crucial to support military operations. The Army integrates the talents and skills of its military and civilian members to form a Total Army.
MajorDuties: Integrates comprehensive knowledge of requirements management operations with the Intelligence Preparation of the Battlefield process and emerging Service and National Intelligence Community cyber warfare doctrine.
Understands the requirements management and all-source intelligence fusion process from tactical- to national-level as well as collection system capabilities and limitations.

Maintains expert knowledge of the requirements management process and methodology as it pertains to threat analysis, and forecasting methodologies and the production of focused and actionable intelligence.
Leverage unique automation systems and requirements databases employed by various organizations and entities to include joint, federal law enforcement, and National Intelligence Community agencies.

Develop and write the organizational requirements plan and coordinate this effort with counterparts at numerous levels of effort to include theater Combatant Commands, Army Service Component Commands, and national intelligence organizations.
Analyze production requirements to determine their validity and relevance, and then appropriately synchronize and integrate these requirements within the production process.

Provide advice and counsel, develop job descriptions, prepare yearly evaluations for civilian and military employees, interview and evaluate candidates for positions, and ensures employee development with both formal and on-the-job training.
Plan workflow and make work assignments, adjusting workloads and adapting or modifying procedures to alleviate backlogs or delays.

Exercise authority to commit Requirements Management resources and obligate the Requirements Management to new directions or courses of action responding to Army, federal law enforcement, and national-level requests for intelligence support.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: This position has a Basic Requirement for the 1550: Bachelor's degree in computer science or bachelor's degree with 30 semester hours in a combination of mathematics, statistics, and computer science. At least 15 of the 30 semester hours must have included any combination of statistics and mathematics that included differential and integral calculus. All academic degrees and course work must be from accredited or pre-accredited institutions. *NOTE: Failure to provide transcripts will result in you being rated ineligible for this position. The experience described in your resume will be evaluated and screened from the Office of Personnel Management's (OPMs) basic qualifications requirements. See: Computer Science Series 1550 for OPM qualification standards, competencies and specialized experience needed to perform the duties of the position as described in the MAJOR DUTIES and QUALIFICATIONS sections of this announcement by 10/19/2026 Applicant must have directly applicable experience that demonstrates the possession of the knowledge, skills, abilities and competencies necessary for immediate success in the position. Qualifying experience may have been acquired in any public or private sector job, but will clearly demonstrate past experience in the application of the particular competencies/knowledge, skills and abilities necessary to successfully perform the duties of the position. You must have specialized experience sufficient to demonstrate that you have acquired all the competencies necessary to perform at a level equivalent in difficulty, responsibility, and complexity to the next lower grade (GS/GG-12) in the Federal service and are prepared to take on greater responsibility. Generally, this would include one year or more of such specialized experience. Specialized experience for this position includes: Applying statistical and general-purpose programming languages (e.g., Python, R, SQL, and C++) to write clean code and build structured data pipelines for advanced data analysis. Implementing programming languages (e.g, C++, SQL, Python, R and other computational languages) to develop complex queries for the support of reporting and advanced analytical and machine learning capabilities. Utilizing natural language processing, text mining, machine learning techniques, and predictive modeling (including decision trees and regression) to transform large volumes of unstructured data into actionable, structured intelligence that supports risk mitigation. Integrating artificial intelligence and data architecture models seamlessly with secure cloud and enterprise IT infrastructure. Utilizing a strong mathematical foundation, specifically linear algebra, calculus, and statistics, to apply rigorous scientific and quantitative methods to evaluate data reliability, perform detailed risk assessments, and design automated data labeling workflows. Specifically you will be evaluated on the following competencies: Artificial Intelligence: This competency requires knowledge of the principles, methods, and tools used to design systems that perform human intelligence functions. Data Analysis: This competency involves the ability to analyze, model, and transform data to highlight useful information, suggest recommendations and conclusions, and support senior leader decision-making. Programming: This competency is the skill to implement design solutions and apply programming languages across multiple platforms and development frameworks. Systems Design: This competency entails the ability to design and evaluate software and hardware and develop enterprise and solution architectures that meet user needs and optimize performance, using applicable principles, methods, and tools. Risk Management: This competency requires knowledge of the principles, methods, and tools used for risk assessment and mitigation, including assessment of failures and their consequences.

Details.JobSummary: DCSA Acquisition and Technology, National Background Investigation Services (NBIS) is seeking a Computer Scientist/Data Engineer (GG-13). The incumbent will serve as a technical advisor, developing advanced AI/ML, NLP, and cloud data architectures to safeguard the federal workforce. This role requires strong programming skills (Python/SQL) and containerization expertise. Visit www.dcsa.mil to learn more about DCSA.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Our Mission Through vetting, industry engagement, education, and counterintelligence and insider threat support, secure the trustworthiness of the United States Government's workforce, the integrity of its cleared contractor support, and the uncompromised nature of its technologies, services, and supply chains. Our Vision DCSA's elite security experts illuminate national security risks to empower faster, smarter decision-making that protects American innovation and resilience to enable mission success. DCSA Strategic Execution Plan The Defense Counterintelligence and Security Agency stands at the intersection of government-wide trusted workforce, national security, and industrial base protection. Guided by the Secretary of War's National Defense Strategy, Deputy Secretary's Warfighting Acquisition Transformation efforts, and Trusted Workforce 2.0, our mission is to deliver data-driven, threat-informed, and customer-trusted security services at scale. The FY2026 - 2028 DCSA Strategic Execution Plan defines six strategic priorities for the agency: Deliver NBIS Deploy NI2 to Modernize Industrial Security Modernize and Sustain Trusted Workforce Determinations Rebuild the Workforce Compact Operate as a Customer-Centric Business Drive Audit-Ready Integration and Agency Efficiency with AI
MajorDuties: As a COMPUTER SCIENTIST you will be responsible for the following duties: Performs professional work in computer science, that may include data science, intelligence, artificial intelligence/machine learning (AI/ML), system analysis, risk analysis, predictive analysis and computer simulation. Serves as a catalyst for creative engineering/computer scientist thinking to integrate new technology capabilities and opportunities to develop more effective and responsive intelligence. Creates unprecedented approaches, analytical tools and methods to analyze unique situations and draw accurate and significant conclusions. Plans, describes and/or develops computer programs required to keep existing software responsive to constant changing data requirements. Implements strategies for system development and analysis, operational logistics, project funding/budgeting, project cost, schedule and performance management. The Office Under Secretary of Defense for Intelligence and Security established a Targeted Local Market Supplement (TLMS) for certain Science, Technology, Engineering, Mathematics, and Cyber positions within the Defense Civilian Intelligence Personnel System. Eligibility for the TLMS is based on cyber work roles within certain occupational series and on the work performed. This vacancy is designated as a STEM and/or Cyber position and pay for the incumbent will be based on the STEM and Cyber Pay Table.

Qualifying experience may have been acquired in any public or private sector job, but will clearly demonstrate past experience in the application of the particular competencies or knowledge, skills, and abilities necessary to successfully perform the duties of the position. Such experience is typically in or directly related to the work of the position to be filled. Qualifying experience would be demonstrated by supporting Unified Capabilities (UC) and Voice Video over Internet Protocol (VVoIP) systems to support continuous services across networks; sustaining collaboration components for communications routing and required compliance configurations; troubleshooting service incidents by conducting technical diagnostics, service restoration, and proactive system monitoring; providing technical guidance regarding United Capabilities to customers and support staff. The specialized experience must include, or be supplemented by, information technology related experience (paid or unpaid experience and/or completion of specific, intensive training, as appropriate) which demonstrates each of the four competencies, as defined: Attention to Detail - Is thorough when performing work and conscientious about attending to detail. Examples of IT-related experience demonstrating this competency include: completing thorough and accurate work independently, even in the most difficult or stressful situations; occasionally reviewing work completed by others. Customer Service - Works with clients and customers (that is, any individuals who use or receive the services or products that your work unit produces, including the general public, individuals who work in the agency, other agencies, or organizations outside the Government) to assess their needs, provide information or assistance, resolve their problems, or satisfy their expectations; knows about available products and services; is committed to providing quality products and services. Examples of IT-related experience demonstrating this competency include: resolving routine and non-routine problems, questions, or complaints; developing and maintaining strong, mutually supportive working relationships with customers; conducting evaluation of support to determine quality of services and customer satisfaction, and recommending procedural changes based on customer need or changes in policy and/or regulation. Oral Communication - Expresses information (for example, ideas or facts) to individuals or groups effectively, taking into account the audience and nature of the information (for example, technical, sensitive, controversial); makes clear and convincing oral presentations; listens to others, attends to nonverbal cues, and responds appropriately. Examples of IT-related experience demonstrating this competency include: convincingly conveying complex information to customers; presenting thoughts that are well-organized and demonstrating confidence in the facts and ideas; adjusting style when working with individuals with different levels of understanding; using various methods to explain and convey information. Problem Solving - Identifies problems; determines accuracy and relevance of information; uses sound judgment to generate and evaluate alternatives, and to make recommendations. Examples of IT-related experience demonstrating this competency include: solving complex or sensitive problems by developing and proposing strategic alternatives; identifying possible conflicts and shared benefits; helping team anticipate problems and identifying and evaluating potential sources of information; providing feedback and coaching to others to help solve problems; engaging appropriate stakeholders when developing solutions in order to understand and incorporate multiple perspectives and needs; evaluating the effectiveness of decisions and adjusting future decisions as appropriate.

Details.JobSummary: About the Position: This position is a DOD Cyber Excepted Service (CES) personnel system position in the Excepted Service under 10 USC 1599f. Employees occupying CES positions are in the Excepted Service and must adhere to U.S. Code, Title 10, as well as Department of Defense Instruction 1400.25. This position is located at the Regional Cyber Center Europe in Wiesbaden, Germany. The initial length of this overseas tour is 36 months with possible extensions up to 5 years.

MajorDuties: Supports the delivery and reliability of Unified Capabilities (UC) services—including enterprise voice, video, and collaboration tools—to ensure effective communication across the organization.
Uses available monitoring tools and automation capabilities to track system health, maintain accurate configuration information, and support proactive service management.
Monitors and evaluates system performance, identifying trends, issues, and improvement areas to help maintain consistent service quality and user experience.
Performs ongoing security, configuration, and compliance checks on network systems, applying organizational policies and required standards to maintain a secure operational environment.
Leads troubleshooting and service restoration efforts for UC-related issues, coordinating with technical teams to resolve incidents efficiently and prevent future disruptions.
Develops and maintains operational procedures, documentation, and user guidance for UC and network services, and provides input to leadership on system enhancements and technology updates.

The degree must be in a major field of study (at least at the baccalaureate level) that is appropriate for the position. or Combination of education and experience: Courses equivalent to a major field of study (30 semester hours) as shown in paragraph A above, plus additional education or appropriate experience. *NOTE: Failure to provide transcripts will result in you being rated ineligible for this position. Qualifying experience may have been acquired in any public or private sector job, but will clearly demonstrate past experience in the application of the particular competencies/knowledge, skills and abilities necessary to successfully perform the duties of the position. You must have specialized experience sufficient to demonstrate that you have acquired all the competencies necessary to perform at a level equivalent in difficulty, responsibility, and complexity to the next lower grade GS/GG-05 in the Federal service and are prepared to take on greater responsibility. Generally, this would include one year or more of such specialized experience. Specialized experience for this position includes: GG-07 - Applying foundational statistical methods (e.g. regression, decision trees, or probability) using basic mathematics, including logarithms, trigonometry, linear algebra, calculus, statistics and operational analysis. Conducting basic risk assessments. Assisting with statistical and general-purpose programming languages for data analysis. Writing basic algorithms leveraging R, Python, or SQL/NoSQL to support the development or testing of analytical models, and explaining the results to teammates. You must have specialized experience sufficient to demonstrate that you have acquired all the competencies necessary to perform at a level equivalent in difficulty, responsibility, and complexity to the next lower grade GS/GG-07 in the Federal service and are prepared to take on greater responsibility. Generally, this would include one year or more of such specialized experience. Specialized experience for this position includes: GG-09 - Applying statistical methods (e.g. regression, decision trees, or probability) using basic mathematics, including logarithms, trigonometry, linear algebra, calculus, statistics and operational analysis. Conducting standard risk assessments. Applying statistical and general-purpose programming languages for data analysis. Leading the development of algorithms leveraging R, Python, or SQL/NoSQL. Specifically you will be evaluated on the following competencies: Data Mining - Computing process of discovering patterns in a large data set involving methods at the intersection of machine learning, statistics, and database systems. Data Management - Knowledge of the principles, procedures, and tools of data management, such as modeling techniques, data backup, data recovery, data dictionaries, data warehousing, data mining, data disposal, and data standardization processes. Software and Programming - Leverage and optimize the use of existing OIG specific software (such as Cloudera Data Platform, Cloudera Data Flow (Apache Nifi), Tableau, DataWalk), while recommending future software mix. Understand a variety of programming languages (such as Java/Javascript, Scala, Python, C/C#/C++, R) as needed to meet software and business needs. Understand a variety of data warehousing platforms (such as Cloudera/Hive, Oracle, SQL, MySQL, NoSQL), big data software (such as Tableau, DataWalk, Apache Hadoop/Spark, ArcGIS), and data science project management and version control applications (such as JIRA, Agile). Qualitative / Quantitative Analysis - Developing and applying quantitative and qualitative analytic methods to identify, collect, process, and analyze large data sets.

Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Our Mission Through vetting, industry engagement, education, and counterintelligence and insider threat support, secure the trustworthiness of the United States Government's workforce, the integrity of its cleared contractor support, and the uncompromised nature of its technologies, services, and supply chains. Our Vision DCSA's elite security experts illuminate national security risks to empower faster, smarter decision-making that protects American innovation and resilience to enable mission success. DCSA Strategic Execution Plan The Defense Counterintelligence and Security Agency stands at the intersection of government-wide trusted workforce, national security, and industrial base protection. Guided by the Secretary of War's National Defense Strategy, Deputy Secretary's Warfighting Acquisition Transformation efforts, and Trusted Workforce 2.0, our mission is to deliver data-driven, threat-informed, and customer-trusted security services at scale. The FY2026 - 2028 DCSA Strategic Execution Plan defines six strategic priorities for the agency: Deliver NBIS Deploy NI2 to Modernize Industrial Security Modernize and Sustain Trusted Workforce Determinations Rebuild the Workforce Compact Operate as a Customer-Centric Business Drive Audit-Ready Integration and Agency Efficiency with AI
MajorDuties: This position may be filled at either GG-07 or GG-09 grade level, please indicate the grade for which you want to be considered. Incumbent may be advanced non-competitively to the established target grade upon meeting developmental benchmarks, performance requirements, and other requirements, as applicable established for the career program or specifically for the incumbent. As a Data Scientist you will be responsible for the following duties: Performs professional work in data science, intelligence, artificial intelligence/machine learning (AI/ML), system analysis, risk analysis, predictive analysis and computer simulation. Applies analytic methods such as regression, decision tree and statistical probability to improve data reliability and quality. Identifies, collects and analyzes data to effectively support and advance projects or programs. Uncover and explain actionable insights from data by combining scientific method, math and statistics, specialized programming, advanced analytics, AI, and storytelling to major organizations, government officials and key stakeholders. Collaborate with team members and stakeholders to ensure data accuracy and consistent reporting. Implements strategies for system development and analysis, operational logistics, project funding/budgeting, project cost, schedule and performance management. Manages and plans sequence of operations on a regular basis for assigned elements. The Office Under Secretary of Defense for Intelligence and Security established a Targeted Local Market Supplement (TLMS) for certain Science, Technology, Engineering, Mathematics, and Cyber positions within the Defense Civilian Intelligence Personnel System. Eligibility for the TLMS is based on cyber work roles within certain occupational series and on the work performed. This vacancy is designated as a STEM and/or Cyber position and pay for the incumbent will be based on the STEM and Cyber Pay Table.

Qualifying experience may have been acquired in any public or private sector job, but will clearly demonstrate past experience in the application of the particular competencies/knowledge, skills and abilities necessary to successfully perform the duties of the position. You must have specialized experience sufficient to demonstrate that you have acquired all the competencies necessary to perform at a level equivalent in difficulty, responsibility, and complexity to the next lower grade (GS/GG-05) in the Federal service and are prepared to take on greater responsibility. Generally, this would include one year or more of such specialized experience. Specialized experience for this position includes: GG-07 - Gathering, planning, implementing and communicating basic information technology policies, ideas, programs and processes effectively to customers, technical personnel, management and senior leadership. Managing the basic principles, methods and techniques of information technology to accomplish baseline assessments, contingency planning and disaster recovery. Applying basic Agile Methodologies and project management principles, processes, procedures, planning and activity development using the SCRUM process. Architecting and designing within the Amazon Web Services (AWS) Elastic Cloud Compute environment, including basic network design. Utilizing basic information technology principles, methods, and tools to assess the effectiveness and practicality of systems while dealing with ordinary and recurring problems. You must have specialized experience sufficient to demonstrate that you have acquired all the competencies necessary to perform at a level equivalent in difficulty, responsibility, and complexity to the next lower grade (GS/GG-07) in the Federal service and are prepared to take on greater responsibility. Generally, this would include one year or more of such specialized experience. Specialized experience for this position includes: GG-09 - Gathering, planning, implementing and communicating intermediate information technology policies, ideas, programs and processes effectively to customers, technical personnel, management and senior leadership. Managing intermediate principles, methods and techniques of information technology to accomplish baseline assessments, contingency planning and disaster recovery. Applying intermediate Agile Methodologies and project management principles, processes, procedures, planning and activity development using the SCRUM process. Architecting and designing within the Amazon Web Services (AWS) Elastic Cloud Compute environment, including intermediate network design. Utilizing intermediate information technology principles, methods, and tools to assess the effectiveness and practicality of systems while dealing with ordinary and recurring problems. Specifically you will be evaluated on the following competencies: Requirements Analysis: Knowledge of the principles and methods to identify, analyze, specify, design, and manage functional and infrastructure requirements; includes translating functional requirements into technical requirements used for logical design or presenting alternative technologies or approaches. Project Management: Knowledge of the principles, methods, or tools for developing, scheduling, coordinating, and managing projects and resources, including monitoring and inspecting costs, work, and contractor performance. Customer Service: Works with clients and customers (that is, any individuals who use or receive the services or products that your work unit produces, including the general public, individuals who work in the agency, other agencies, or organizations outside the Government) to assess their needs, provide information or assistance, resolve their problems, or satisfy their expectations; knows about available products and services; is committed to providing quality products and services. Software Development: Knowledge of the principles, methods, and tools for designing, developing, and testing software in a given environment. In addition to meeting qualifications, your application package must reflect the applicable experience to meet the Individual Occupational Requirements for the 2210, series as listed below: Attention to Detail - Is thorough when performing work and conscientious about attending to detail. Customer Service - Works with clients and customers (that is, any individuals who use or receive the services or products that your work unit produces, including the general public, individuals who work in the agency, other agencies, or organizations outside the Government) to assess their needs, provide information or assistance, resolve their problems, or satisfy their expectations; knows about available products and services; is committed to providing quality products and services. Oral Communication - Expresses information (for example, ideas or facts) to individuals or groups effectively, taking into account the audience and nature of the information (for example, technical, sensitive, controversial); makes clear and convincing oral presentations; listens to others, attends to nonverbal cues, and responds appropriately. Problem Solving - Identifies problems; determines accuracy and relevance of information; uses sound judgment to generate and evaluate alternatives, and to make recommendations.

Details.JobSummary: Join the Defense Counterintelligence and Security Agency (DCSA) as a developmental Product Owner. In this entry-level position, you will work under direct supervision to manage product backlogs, translate user needs into technical requirements, and coordinate Agile IT development teams. Apply today to launch your federal IT career!
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Our Mission Through vetting, industry engagement, education, and counterintelligence and insider threat support, secure the trustworthiness of the United States Government's workforce, the integrity of its cleared contractor support, and the uncompromised nature of its technologies, services, and supply chains. Our Vision DCSA's elite security experts illuminate national security risks to empower faster, smarter decision-making that protects American innovation and resilience to enable mission success. DCSA Strategic Execution Plan The Defense Counterintelligence and Security Agency stands at the intersection of government-wide trusted workforce, national security, and industrial base protection. Guided by the Secretary of War's National Defense Strategy, Deputy Secretary's Warfighting Acquisition Transformation efforts, and Trusted Workforce 2.0, our mission is to deliver data-driven, threat-informed, and customer-trusted security services at scale. The FY2026 - 2028 DCSA Strategic Execution Plan defines six strategic priorities for the agency: Deliver NBIS Deploy NI2 to Modernize Industrial Security Modernize and Sustain Trusted Workforce Determinations Rebuild the Workforce Compact Operate as a Customer-Centric Business Drive Audit-Ready Integration and Agency Efficiency with AI
MajorDuties: This position may be filled at either GG-07 or GG-09 grade level, please indicate the grade for which you want to be considered. Incumbent may be advanced non-competitively to the established target grade upon meeting developmental benchmarks, performance requirements, and other requirements, as applicable established for the career program or specifically for the incumbent. As a IT Specialist (PLCYPLN) you will be responsible for the following duties: Serves as the Government Scrum Master/Product Owner of an agile team prioritizing work, managing schedules for IT development teams, and utilizing agile tools and best practices. Translates business requirements into technical solutions and converts user requirements to technical requirements while managing the product backlog. Prioritizes projects and tasks for contractors while facilitating project initiations, approval processes, change management, and deployment activities. Oversees contractor development activities to enforce DoD policy, standards, and security principles, ensuring the quality and integrity of delivered products. Maintains relationships with business partners and acts as a liaison between cross-functional Information Technology teams and customers to understand and meet expectations. Provides technology roadmaps for consistent implementation and migration of legacy applications to new technology tools and cloud solutions. Ensures the rigorous application of information security/information assurance policies, principles, and practices in the delivery of planning and management services. The Office Under Secretary of Defense for Intelligence and Security established a Targeted Local Market Supplement (TLMS) for certain Science, Technology, Engineering, Mathematics, and Cyber positions within the Defense Civilian Intelligence Personnel System. Eligibility for the TLMS is based on cyber work roles within certain occupational series and on the work performed. This vacancy is designated as a STEM and/or Cyber position and pay for the incumbent will be based on the STEM and Cyber Pay Table.
Details.Education: If substituting education for experience at the GG-07 level, you must possess 1 Full Year of graduate level education. If substituting education for experience at the GG-09 level, you must possess a masters or equivalent degree OR 2 full years of progressively higher graduate education leading to such a degree, OR LL.B. or J.D., if related. If substituting or combining education for experience, transcripts MUST be provided. Failure to provide transcripts will result in you being rated ineligible for this position. Superior Academic Achievement does not apply to DCIPS positions. Foreign Education: For further information, click on the following link: https://sites.ed.gov/international/recognition-of-foreign-qualifications/
Details.Evaluations: You will be evaluated based on how well you meet the qualifications listed in this vacancy announcement. Your qualifications will be evaluated based on your application materials (e.g., resume, supporting documents), the responses you provide on the application questionnaire. TECHNICAL ASSESSMENT: Your complete application package (resume/supporting documentation and online technical questionnaire) will be used to determine whether you meet the job qualifications listed on this announcement. If you are basically qualified for this job, your resume and supporting documentation will be compared to your responses on the online questionnaire. If you are found to be among the top candidates, you will be referred to the selecting official for employment consideration. You should list any relevant performance appraisals and incentive awards in your resume as that information may be taken into consideration during the selection process. If selected, you may be required to provide supporting documentation. Top ranked candidates will be referred to the selecting official for further review and consideration. A review of your resume and supporting documentation will be made and compared against your responses to the Assessment Questionnaire to determine if you are qualified for this job. If your resume is incomplete or does not support the responses provided in the Assessment Questionnaire, or if you fail to submit all required documentation, you will be rated 'ineligible', 'not qualified'. Please follow all instructions carefully. Errors or omissions may affect your rating or consideration for employment. MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: QUALIFICATIONS REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS: Successful candidates should demonstrate, at a level appropriate to the rank sought: - A Masters or Terminal Degree - Academic or professional expertise relevant to contemporary warfighting together with broad judgment beyond a narrow specialty. - Ability to build cadet understanding across tactical, operational, and strategic levels as one coherent warfighting system. - Ability to cultivate an Airman and Guardian perspective while integrating joint and multidomain effects. - Knowledge of high-end conflict, including sensing, autonomy, contested space, cyber and electronic warfare, long-range effects, contested command and control, and AI. - Ability to design or employ immersive wargaming, simulations, digital environments, decision exercises, and after-action processes integrating adversary behavior, technology, theory, strategy, and national purpose. - Knowledge of effective undergraduate teaching and ability to collaborate across disciplines and professional communities while maintaining academic, operational, and professional currency. Associate Professors and Professors should additionally demonstrate progressively greater academic leadership. ACADEMIC DISCIPLINES: Relevant fields may include military, war, strategic, security, or national-security studies; military history; international relations; political science; defense policy; airpower; spacepower; cyber; AI; autonomous systems; electronic warfare; information operations; intelligence; operational planning or art; joint operations; wargaming; modeling and simulation; operations research; military innovation; defense technology; logistics; acquisition; professional military education; or another closely related field supporting Warfighting. DESIRED QUALIFICATIONS: - Excellent undergraduate, graduate, or professional military teaching, especially in interdisciplinary or applied settings. - Experience with military theory or history, strategy, operational art, joint or all-domain operations, airpower, spacepower, cyber, or related fields. - Experience designing or employing immersive wargaming, scenario-based instruction, simulation, digital operational environments, decision exercises, or comparable experiential learning. - Experience with high-end warfighting, adaptive adversaries, or emerging technologies such as AI, autonomy, contested space, cyber, or electronic warfare. - Relevant operational, command or staff, government, defense, intelligence, industry, professional military education, curriculum-development, or research experience. Applicants will be evaluated on their ability to contribute to the teaching-centered, integrated mission of SIGS, including: - Academic or professional preparation, warfighting expertise and breadth, and undergraduate or professional military teaching effectiveness. - Ability to build a coherent Airman and Guardian mental model across tactical, operational, and strategic levels while remaining fully joint and multidomain. - Knowledge of high-end conflict and the emerging character of war, including AI and rapidly evolving technologies. - Experience with immersive wargaming, simulation, digital operational environments, scenario-based instruction, or comparable applied learning. - Ability to integrate military theory, history, technology, strategy, policy, ethics, law, operational practice, and national purpose. - Cadet mentorship, intellectual, operational or professional engagement, service, collaboration, and leadership appropriate to rank. Applicants should submit a curriculum vitae or resume and a cover letter describing how they would contribute to an integrated Warfighting thread; prepare cadets for high-end conflict from a fully joint Airman and Guardian perspective; and use immersive exercises or wargaming to integrate military, technical, humanistic, and strategic judgment. Inquiries about the position should be directed to the Dean, School of Integrated General Studies (SIGS), Dr. Mark N. Jensen, email: mark.jensen@afacademy.af.edu. Please do not email documents or completed applications to this address as they will not be considered.

Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The mission of the United States Air Force Academy is to educate, train, and inspire men and women to become leaders of character, motivated to lead the United States Air Force in service to our nation. USAFA, located just north of Colorado Springs, Colorado, is an undergraduate institution that awards the Bachelor of Science degree. Faculty applications are invited from candidates who can contribute by interacting with cadets, both in and out of the classroom, as instructors and mentors. The student body consists of approximately 4,000 students representing every state and several foreign countries. USAFA faculty is an integrated group of military and civilian educators. The curriculum includes core academic and professional courses, and 27 disciplinary and interdisciplinary majors.
MajorDuties: Major Duties of the Position: Instructor (AD-21): Deliver structured undergraduate general-education instruction within the common curriculum under academic direction. Select and adapt approved instructional materials consistent with common course objectives, evaluate student performance, provide academic advising, maintain professional currency, and participate in assigned course-team, School, and Academy service. Assistant Professor (AD-22): Deliver and assess undergraduate courses within the common curriculum and contribute to their planning and continuous improvement. Assume increasing course leadership and coordination responsibilities, such as serving as a Course Director. Maintain appropriate scholarly or professional engagement while contributing to course teams, School service, and interdisciplinary integration. Associate Professor (AD-23): Provide sustained teaching excellence and lead major multi-section courses or significant curriculum components. Maintain sustained scholarly or professional engagement appropriate to the educational mission. Lead course-team and School-level curriculum and assessment efforts and actively mentor junior faculty. Professor (AD-24 - Nonsupervisory): Provide distinguished instruction and senior academic leadership in the design, integration, and continuous improvement of the common curriculum. Maintain mature scholarly or professional engagement appropriate to the educational mission. Lead major School- and institution-level academic initiatives and mentor and develop faculty colleagues across academic areas. The School of Integrated General Studies (SIGS) provides the common core academic education upon which later specialized disciplinary education builds. It forms cadets as Citizens, Leaders, Warfighters, and Scholars. The SIGS curriculum integrates civics, humanities, arts, and social sciences (CHASS), STEM and Artificial Intelligence, and Warfighting threads. Faculty work across conventional disciplinary boundaries to build a rigorous, ordered, and mission-aligned general education for future Air Force and Space Force officers. The Warfighting thread prepares cadets for the high-end fight through a coherent developmental curriculum rather than separate courses in tactics, operations, and strategy. It builds a cumulative Airman and Guardian mental model: how air, space, and cyber combine with joint and multidomain effects; how tactical actions create operational effects; and how campaigns and strategy serve constitutional authority, political purpose, and the national interest. Military theory and history, contemporary operations, emerging technologies, and immersive wargaming are integrated so cadets repeatedly test and refine their judgment against adaptive adversaries. These are teaching-centered positions. SIGS seeks educators who work beyond a single specialty; connect theory, history, tactics, operations, strategy, technology, human judgment, ethics, law, policy, and national purpose; and cultivate an Airman and Guardian perspective while remaining fully joint. Faculty should prepare cadets to decide well in contested, high-consequence environments. Scholarly, operational, and professional activity supports this mission, but the paramount purpose of these positions is excellent undergraduate teaching and related service supporting a coherent, integrated Warfighting thread.
Details.Education: EDUCATION: If selected, you will be requested to provide original copies of ALL OFFICIAL transcripts for degrees being pursued or obtained (or letter of degree completion if an OFFICIAL transcript is not available due to recent graduation) to support your educational claims as stated in your curriculum vitae. Your transcripts must also reflect the degree awarded/conferred date. Transcripts labeled UNOFFICIAL will not be accepted. However, you must show proof that the education credentials have been deemed to be at least equivalent to that gained in a conventional U.S. education program. It is your responsibility to provide such evidence when applying in the form of an "official" statement of U.S. equivalency from a Department of Education approved (non-federal) agency (i.e. AICE, NACES), who will complete a U.S. Standard of Education Conversion.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: In order to qualify, you must meet the specialized experience requirements described in the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) Qualification Standards for General Schedule Positions, Professional and Scientific Positions. BASIC REQUIREMENT OR INDIVIDUAL OCCUPATIONAL REQUIREMENT: Degree: Mathematics, statistics, computer science, data science or field directly related to the position. The degree must be in a major field of study (at least at the baccalaureate level) that is appropriate for the position. NOTE: You must submit a copy of your transcripts with your application. OR Combination of education and experience: Courses equivalent to a major field of study (30 semester hours) plus additional education or appropriate experience. NOTE: You must submit a copy of your transcripts with your application. In addition to meeting the basic requirement above, to qualify for this position you must also meet the qualification requirements listed below: SPECIALIZED EXPERIENCE: Applicants must have at least one (1) year of specialized experience at the next lower grade GS-13, or equivalent in other pay systems. Examples of specialized experience includes experience of data analyses, mathematics, statistical analysis, modeling/simulation, and/or other scientific concepts, principles, standards, methods, techniques, practices, and procedures. Expertise in data modeling, query authoring and performance tuning with an in-depth understanding of data modeling best practices, relational and graph databases. Skill of advanced, analytical, mathematical, or statistical theories, principles, concepts, methods, and techniques to provide expert judgments concerning the validity of assumptions made and the criteria to evaluate alternatives. Experience working with large and complex data sets and performing extensive analysis of volumes of data and designing and delivering frameworks to facilitate the data development lifecycle and design, implementation integration and maintenance of the pipeline and data warehouse and transitions to cloud-based data solutions. NOTE: Your resume must support the response you select. FEDERAL TIME-IN-GRADE (TIG) REQUIREMENT FOR GENERAL SCHEDULE (GS) POSITIONS: Merit promotion applicants must meet applicable time-in-grade requirements to be considered eligible. One year at the GS-13 level is required to meet the time-in-grade requirements for the GS-14 level. TIG applies if you are in a current GS position or held a GS position within the previous 52 weeks. NOTE: Applicants applying as VEOA candidates who are current GS civil service employees or are prior GS civil service employees within the past 52 weeks must also meet time-in-grade requirements. KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES (KSAs): Your qualifications will be evaluated on the basis of your level of knowledge, skills, abilities and/or competencies in the following areas: 1. In-depth understanding of statistical analysis, data engineering, AI and machine learning, data mining techniques, and predictive modeling. 2. Programming and Data Manipulation: Proficiency in programming languages such as Python, R, or Java, and experience with data manipulation libraries (e.g., Pandas, NumPy). 3. Expert knowledge of statistical techniques, concepts, hypothesis testing, and experimental design sufficient to analyze complex datasets and draw meaningful insights. 4. Knowledge of safety and security regulations, practices, and procedures; Ability to clean, preprocess, and transform data for analysis and modeling. 5. Skill and ability to tailor and present findings and recommendations to all levels, justify and defend decisions and recommendations, and to represent the command at briefings, meetings, or other required functions.6. Ability to collaborate effectively with cross-functional teams, including business analysts, software engineers, and stakeholders; Ability to plan, organize, and direct the functions and staff of a small to medium sized organization. PART-TIME OR UNPAID EXPERIENCE: Credit will be given for appropriate unpaid and or part-time work. You must clearly identify the duties and responsibilities in each position held and the total number of hours per week. VOLUNTEER WORK EXPERIENCE: Refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service Programs (i.e., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student and social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge and skills that can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.

Details.JobSummary: This National Guard position is for a NONDESTRUCTIVE TESTER, Position Description Number D2320000 and is part of the Oregon Air National Guard 142nd Wing, National Guard.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: This position is a Title 32 Excepted Service - Military position. Oregon Air National Guard military service is a condition of employment. The National Guard is the oldest component of the Armed Forces of the United States. Since the earliest American colonial days, citizens have joined together for collective defense. We have a proud tradition of coming to the aid of our friends and neighbors in times of serious emergencies. Join our National Guard team and serve your nation, your states and your community! NATIONAL GUARD MEMBERSHIP IS REQUIRED: This is an excepted service position that requires membership in a compatible military assignment in the National Guard. Selectee will be required to wear the military uniform. Acceptance of an excepted service position constitutes concurrence with these requirements as a condition of employment.
MajorDuties: As a NONDESTRUCTIVE TESTER, WG-3705-10, this position is located in the Aircraft Structural Maintenance Section of an Air National Guard aircraft Maintenance Group, Maintenance Squadron, Fabrication Flight. This is an Air National Guard (ANG) Dual Status Technician position requiring military membership, compatible military skill assignment, and classification. The primary purpose of this position is to inspect aerospace weapon systems components and support equipment for structural integrity using nondestructive inspection methods and performs fluid analysis. 1. Determines test method, and prepares fluids and parts for nondestructive inspection. Interprets nondestructive inspection test results, and provides information about defects to repair center. Performs Oil Spectrometry process and analyzes wear metal content on engine lubricating oil and other fluids, and recommends corrective action. Establishes radiation areas for radiographic operations. Computes and monitors personal exposure areas for radiographic operations, and monitors personnel exposure data. 2. Performs nondestructive inspection on structures, components, and systems. Detects flaws such as cracks, delaminations, voids, processing defects, and heat damage using penetrant, eddy current, magnetic particle, radiographic, optical, Thermography, Shearography and ultrasonic test equipment. Determines metallurgical information of components according to alloy, temper, conductivity, and associated factors. May also serve as Alternate TMDE Monitor, PCAMS, Alternate Equipment Custodian, Alternate Supplies Manager, Alternate Hazardous Waste Monitor, Alternate Hazardous Communication Monitor, Alternate Spill Prevention Monitor, Alternate FOD Monitor, Alternate Radiation Monitor, Alternate Technical Order Monitor, Alternate Precious Metals Monitor, and Training Monitor. 3. Applies magnetic particle and/or liquid penetrant inspection to detect and interpret the relevancy of flaws in a variety of parts. Parts are numerous and varied, and are of ferrous and/or nonferrous metals, and consist of surface or near surface discontinuities in the metal; e.g., fatigue cracks, welding overlap, cold shut, or surface cracks that may stem from internal flaws, such as pipes, inclusions, or forging lap. Sets up each different liquid penetrant or magnetic particle method following Technical Orders (TOs), Time Change Technical Orders (TCTOs), or Work Control Documents (WCDs), or Nondestructive Testing Instructions (NDIs). Ensures the equipment and solutions are in compliance with technical guides and quality standards before performing tests and must submit an AFTO 22 if defects in TO's exist or an AF 107 if there is no technical data to accompany the task. Performs all processing tasks; i.e., dipping items in penetrant or magnetic particle baths, washing and drying, magnetizing and demagnetizing ferrous items, and subjecting them to Ultra Violet Black light to detect and evaluate flaws, their nature, size, scope, and exact location. If items are repairable, records test results, and marks defect areas and dimensions. Initiates WCDs that specify the needed repairs. Re-inspects all repairs performed on each component upon their return to the shop. 4. Uses and maintains tools. Maintains bench stock levels of parts, materials, tools, and equipment at prescribed levels. Uses tools and equipment associated with testing being conducted in the shop, as well as hand and power tools to do the work. 5. Utilizes safety practices and procedures following established safety rules and regulations to maintain a safe and clean work environment. Uses and assures proper fit of required Personal Protective Equipment and clothing. Follows federal and state rules when storing, using, handling, labeling, and disposing of hazardous materials and waste in accordance with environmental standards. Performs clean-up duties, such as cleaning equipment, sweeping, straightening, and lining up tools and other property in the assigned area. 6. Maintains records and documents actions. Manually documents actions taken or enters information into an automated system. Obtains required coordination and signatures. 7. Performs other duties as assigned. *The above description only mentions a limited amount of the position's official duties. For a full comprehensive document that covers all the duties of the position, please contact one of the Recruitment Specialists at the bottom of the announcement.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: The experience described in your resume will be evaluated and screened from the Office of Personnel Management's (OPMs) basic qualifications requirements. See: https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/classification-qualifications/competency-based-policy/general-schedule/2200/2210-competency-based-policy/competency-based-qualification-standard/ for OPM qualification standards, competencies and specialized experience needed to perform the duties of the position as described in the MAJOR DUTIES and QUALIFICATIONS sections of this announcement by 10/19/2026 Applicant must have directly applicable experience that demonstrates the possession of the knowledge, skills, abilities and competencies necessary for immediate success in the position. Qualifying experience may have been acquired in any public or private sector job, but will clearly demonstrate past experience in the application of the particular competencies/knowledge, skills and abilities necessary to successfully perform the duties of the position. You must have specialized experience sufficient to demonstrate that you have acquired all the competencies necessary to perform at a level equivalent in difficulty, responsibility, and complexity to the next lower grade GS/GG-12 in the Federal service and are prepared to take on greater responsibility. Generally, this would include one year or more of such specialized experience. Specialized experience for this position includes: Implementing principles, methods, and techniques of IT assessment, planning, management, monitoring and evaluation so that baseline assessments, contingency planning and disaster recovery are accomplished. Applying IT planning and policy frameworks to gather and translate complex business requirements, communicating technical strategies and controversial programs to technical teams and senior leadership. Utilizing Agile Methodologies and the SCRUM process to apply project management principles, processes, procedures, planning and activity development while establishing baseline Information Technology assessments and executing contingency/disaster recovery planning. Managing systems lifecycle concepts to plan, develop, implement, operate and maintain complex IT systems while successfully communicating high-stakes, technical roadmaps to senior leadership. Enforcing information security and assurance principles (including security architecture, vulnerability remediation, and national security regulations) across enterprise systems and contractor development activities. Specifically you will be evaluated on the following competencies: Information Technology Policy and Planning: Develop and promulgate Information Technology strategy, policy, guidance, and plans. Monitor to ensure consistency and compliance. Project Management: Knowledge of the principles, methods, or tools for developing, scheduling, coordinating, and managing projects and resources, including monitoring and inspecting costs, work, and contractor performance. Information Technology Life Cycle Management: Plan, develop and/or manage processes across the information systems/services life cycle to ensure Information Technology capabilities meet current and future organizational and enterprise missions. Planning and Evaluating: Organizes work, sets priorities, and determines resource requirements; determines short- or long-term goals and strategies to achieve them; coordinates with other organizations or parts of the organization to accomplish goals; monitors progress and evaluates outcomes. Cyber Security: Support protection of the confidentiality, integrity, non-repudiation, and availability of systems, networks, and data through planning, analysis, development, penetration testing, access control, implementation, maintenance, and enhancement of information security systems, programs, policies, procedures, and tools.
